### A01
Decision: P may be released now, because its provider was never invoked. Q stays reserved until its provider actually settles and AGP disposes its retained request/result. Cancellation, revocation or the session ending does not release Q. R stays reserved while its result is waiting. Its slot is released once, when AGP actually disposes that owned result. In the terminal sequence, R counts as "actually disposable" work and can be released in that turn. Q cannot.

Document support:
QUOTE: "A reservation whose invocation permit is revoked before the provider is called can be released immediately."
QUOTE: "Permit revoked before invocation, or evaluation settles and AGP disposes its retained request/result"
QUOTE: "After invocation, no reset merely because the session ended or the abort signal fired"
QUOTE: "Its capacity remains reserved while that result is waiting, preventing an unbounded queue of settled results behind the executor."
QUOTE: "Release only uninvoked evaluation permits and actually disposable retained results; keep reservations for started unsettled evaluations and other genuinely retained resources."

Inference or gap: The design does not say whether an ordinary (non-terminal) cleanup checkpoint must dispose R immediately or may defer it. It only says R is released on actual disposal.

### A02
Decision: No. The late rejection may not fault the replacement and may not release the replacement's reservation. Authority comes from the exact controller incarnation, admission kind, token and deadline, checked in a short executor turn behind the runtime gate. Sharing a peer identity confers no authority. The old completion is stale and has no session authority. The only permitted handling is to dispose the old evaluation's retained work and release the old evaluation's own reservation exactly once.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Route the prepared completion through a short executor turn that checks the runtime authority gate, controller identity, admission kind, token and deadline"
QUOTE: "Apply the same exact-token requirement to success, rejection, fault and expiry"
QUOTE: "On eventual provider settlement, dispose the retained work and release its reservation exactly once; stale success and stale failure have the same lack of authority."
QUOTE: "Revocation detaches the result's session-effect target; a late observer retains only bounded work-accounting state, not a closure that keeps the controller and channel alive."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A03
Decision: Not permitted. Result normalization (property access, cloning, provider-controlled callbacks) must happen outside the executor. It produces bounded, owned, immutable data before the short guarded executor turn. Abort-event delivery must also stay outside the executor, and is requested only after authority has been revoked or detached. Both can run application code. The serialized prepare-to-install sequence forbids external callbacks between preparation and installation.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Normalize a potentially current provider result outside the executor into bounded owned immutable data"
QUOTE: "Property access, cloning and provider-controlled callbacks must not become application code running inside the executor."
QUOTE: "Provider calls and abort-event delivery both stay outside the executor because either can run application code."
QUOTE: "without yielding, recursive publication or external callbacks between preparation and installation"

Inference or gap: NONE

### A04
Decision: The plan's fate depends on the boundary rule. If a deadline equal to now counts as expired, the final guard discards the ordinary plan before any effects. The permit is not consumed and cannot be carried across an asynchronous boundary. No route revision, RIB change or ACK occurs. The missing timer input does not matter, because deadline validity is checked directly, not inferred from timer delivery. Room in numeric preflight does not authorize the commit either. The design does not say whether the coordinator must itself commit the expiry transition in this same serialized turn, or leave it to the timer owner. "Discarded or rebuilt" is the only instruction given.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Deadline validity is checked again at result application, not inferred from whether the timer callback has run."
QUOTE: "Expired/stale preparation is discarded or rebuilt before effects; the permit never crosses an asynchronous boundary"
QUOTE: "On expiry or terminal disposition, revoke authority first, cancel its timer, detach its effect target and request cooperative cancellation outside the executor; proceed with session cleanup without joining the provider."

Inference or gap: Missing rule: the design does not define whether a deadline equal to now is elapsed (inclusive or exclusive). Missing rule: no owner is named for advancing the session (committing the expiry/terminal transition) within the turn whose final guard observes expiry.

### A05
Decision: In the tie case, both deadlines have elapsed, so continued admission authority is not allowed. Some timeout terminal is authorized. Which cause wins is not decided: "earlier applicable OPEN deadline wins" covers only a strictly earlier OPEN deadline, and timer delivery order is not authority. In the early-wake case, no expiry transition is authorized. The callback must recheck the monotonic deadline, and the timer presumably reschedules under its generation. The evaluation remains current.

Document support:
QUOTE: "the earlier applicable OPEN deadline still wins"
QUOTE: "Use monotonic elapsed time, tokened timer generations and deadline checks at invocation and commit."
QUOTE: "Node documents delayed callback execution and delay coercion, so a callback's scheduling is not proof that a deadline remains valid (Node timer semantics)."
QUOTE: "Chunk oversized host timer delays and round positive fractional remainders upward; cancellation of a scheduled callback alone is not a stale-generation guard."

Inference or gap: Missing rule: no tie-break between equal admission and OPEN deadlines. Inference: an early wake re-arms rather than expires; rescheduling is implied by the chunking rule but not stated explicitly.

### A06
Decision: The design does not determine the absolute deadline. It requires one teardown budget, started when the terminal cause commits (t=100), that covers notification write, close and terminal drain. It never names transportCloseTimeoutMs or transportWriteTimeoutMs and gives no budget value or formula. Candidates such as 100+900=1000 or 100+2400=2500 would be guesses. Close does not receive a fresh 900 ms allowance at t=850: the single budget started at commit, and a signal given only to a later close cannot be the bound. Migration consequence: whether the two existing settings combine, become sub-limits or are replaced by a new effective teardown setting is unspecified. That needs a configuration decision before implementation.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Start one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits."
QUOTE: "The teardown deadline must cover every wait it owns"
QUOTE: "The deadline actively stops the writer and aborts the channel even if notification write or graceful close has not settled; a signal passed only to a later `close()` call cannot bound an earlier wait."

Inference or gap: Missing rule: no teardown-budget value, no setting name, and no mapping from the existing write/close timeouts; the resolved-settings table omits it.

### A07
Decision: Detachment may not disable the cleanup guard. The terminal sequence hands still-needed reader/channel cleanup to its existing bounded cleanup owner, and those tasks cannot restore authority. Restarting D is not authorized: the single teardown budget begins when the terminal cause commits, and detachment is not a new commit of that session's cause. The write timeout may not replace the committed protocol cause, because one terminal cause wins. The reader must still consume the transport terminal evidence.

Document support:
QUOTE: "One terminal cause wins"
QUOTE: "Start one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits."
QUOTE: "transfer still-needed reader/channel cleanup to its existing bounded cleanup owner"
QUOTE: "These tasks cannot restore live authority, schedule retry or publish operations changes, even if they settle immediately."

Inference or gap: The design has no explicit "detachment does not restart the deadline" sentence; non-restart is inferred from the single-budget and handoff rules.

### A08
Decision: No to both. Draining stops at the head that started the new admission, until that result arrives. The new ordinary route ACK joins the same FIFO behind the backlog and cannot bypass it; only terminal commands bypass. The head's queue reservation is removed (dequeued) only in the dispatch turn that transfers the input to the reserved evaluation record of the new admission. Until then the head stays reserved in place, without being moved to a separate task queue.

Document support:
QUOTE: "processing a queued command that starts another admission stops that drain until the new result arrives."
QUOTE: "New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it."
QUOTE: "Use the queue's head without releasing its reservation while the synchronous dispatch turn prepares the command; do not dequeue into a separate task queue."
QUOTE: "Dequeue only after dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, including a reserved evaluation record when another admission starts."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A09
Decision: The administrative terminal invalidates the pending token. The queued data command and the credit-bearing command are discarded as semantic work, and their peer-credit grant is not applied. Their continuation-queue reservations are released with that disposal. Returning transport capacity is a separate bound and does not release them. The invoked unsettled provider keeps its work reservation until it settles and is disposed. The sole reader must keep draining the transport's already-accepted FIFO, with no protocol effects, until the transport terminal, and then stop.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Remain runnable through their existing owner; invalidate the pending token when terminal"
QUOTE: "Reading ahead is not permission to apply a queued packet's peer-credit grant early."
QUOTE: "Receive-ring credit and continuation storage are distinct bounds: returning transport capacity must not release the queue's reservation."
QUOTE: "An admitted packet may become semantically inert after a session-fatal event, but the transport's already-accepted FIFO must still be drained; a second reader or an early read cancellation is not the correction."
QUOTE: "Drain without protocol effects until the transport terminal, then stop the sole reader"

Inference or gap: Explicit "discard queued semantic work" appears only for overflow ("discard queued semantic work and drain transport evidence") and numeric terminal ("purge semantic queues"). Applying it to administrative terminal is an inference. Whether credit carried by discarded packets is ever honoured is unstated.

### A10
Decision: The design does not authorize skipping. Its sequence invokes after a committed reservation, and it explicitly requires validating against "an empty subset". That implies an empty-subset invocation is a legitimate case. A skip optimization is neither explicitly forbidden nor allowed. If the provider is invoked, the only valid decision list is empty: exactly one decision per requested tuple, and none were requested.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset."
QUOTE: "the contract requires policy decisions only for routes not already statically rejected"
QUOTE: "returns exactly one decision per requested tuple"

Inference or gap: Missing rule on whether a zero-eligible snapshot may bypass the provider. If it may, the design also does not say what happens to the already-committed reservation in that case.

### A11
Decision: The complete valid list with one policy denial is a normal outcome. The denial is nonfatal, and the result yields one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK. The malformed or incomplete list is rejected without retaining an unbounded copy. It causes no revision, RIB change or ACK, and leaves no partial routing state. Whether the malformed list ends the session is only inferred: it appears to be an admission fault with the existing fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` disposition.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"
QUOTE: "reject invalid shape without retaining an unbounded copy"
QUOTE: "a failed preparation leaves no partial routing state"
QUOTE: "Success, rejection, thrown/invalid result and timer callbacks obey the same exact current-token guard"

Inference or gap: The design does not explicitly classify an invalid route result as a session-terminal admission fault. That classification rests on the existing contract, which is not reproduced here.

### A12
Decision: Available RIB space is decided at the final serialized commit, not reserved at the initial proposal. This is not `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, which refers to the evaluation-work pools before invocation. The design does not say whether a RIB shortfall gives partial acceptance, per-route rejection or a session failure. It requires only that current RIB capacity and complete validation come before the single committed revision and ACK, and that failed preparation leaves no partial state. So the revision is consumed and the ACK authorized only if a complete preparation succeeds against current capacity.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Compute available RIB capacity at the final serialized commit, because other sessions may change it while policy runs; do not reserve a stale global-capacity answer in the initial proposal."
QUOTE: "current RIB capacity and complete validation precede the one committed revision and ACK"
QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`"

Inference or gap: Missing rule: the outcome when allowed routes exceed current RIB capacity. It defers to an existing routing contract that is not stated here.

### A13
Decision: Neither may continue as an ordinary transaction. The unrelated exhaustion goes through the same node-owned coordinator and gate. That sets the host to `Failed` and invalidates all admission result permits, so the prepared identity result gets `already-terminal` and no effects. The queued stop completion must observe the terminal gate. It must not overwrite `Failed`, generate a revision or rearm adjacencies. Owner: the node, which owns the single runtime gate and the commit coordinator. Boundary: no ordinary effect after the terminal gate closes.

Document support:
QUOTE: "The node owns one authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator"
QUOTE: "All runtime operations publications must reach this coordinator, including ones outside admission, so an unrelated counter/event/revision exhaustion revokes admission and acquisition authority too."
QUOTE: "invalidate the node generation, all admission invocation/result permits"
QUOTE: "Already-terminal calls return `already-terminal` and the same frozen capture without effects, increments or another terminal transaction."
QUOTE: "A stop or listener-failure continuation already queued must observe the terminal gate and must not overwrite `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`, generate another revision, or rearm an adjacency."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A14
Decision: Both queries return the same frozen terminal capture. It shows two outstanding evaluations, with the terminal revision and capturedAt T. Later private disposal publishes no new revision, event or counter, and adds no fresh timestamp. A caller can conclude only that two evaluations were unresolved at T. The capture is last-known, not proof that resources are still allocated or have since been freed.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Freeze its resource values, revision and `capturedAt` together; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that same terminal capture, not a new timestamp on old counts."
QUOTE: "Outstanding provider evaluations remain nonzero at that capture when unresolved; later private disposal can release internal reservations but cannot publish a new revision, event or counter."
QUOTE: "The final count is last-known at the terminal capture, not a live promise that resources remain allocated or that cleanup has finished."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A15
Decision: Disposal does not reopen the lifecycle or event subscriptions. Accounting stays live because no numeric-terminal barrier occurred. Inference: the gauge change is a publication through the coordinator, so disposal, not the read-only queries, may advance the revision. Queries perform no mutation and should not advance it. Capture time is not frozen for an ordinary stop, since freezing is defined only for a numeric terminal. That suggests it is live, but this is not stated.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances remain queryable: later settlement may update cleanup gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions."
QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances retain live accounting until an operational-domain terminal barrier actually occurs."
QUOTE: "The current implementation's `#capture` samples wall time afresh even after terminal failure"

Inference or gap: Missing rule: whether a post-stop gauge update consumes a revision, and whether ordinary-stop query capture time is sampled freshly. Both are inferred, not stated.

### A16
Decision: The projection is not necessarily wrong. A never-attempted adjacency blocked on identity capacity is `retry-wait` with a capacity reason, no `retryAt` and no `activeControllerId`. Disabled reconnect does not prevent the initial attempt or its capacity wait. Waiting consumes no attempt and represents no timer. Only identity capacity must open, because there is no remembered route refusal and route pressure alone does not block an identity-only phase. Inference: the reason should be `identity-admission-capacity`, not the combined value.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured"
QUOTE: "`retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`, no `activeControllerId`; `retryAttempt` unchanged"
QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
QUOTE: "At eligibility checks, identity capacity is always required; route capacity is required only when that set includes a local route-capacity refusal."
QUOTE: "Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase"
QUOTE: "`retryAt` is the wall-time projection recorded when a real monotonic backoff timer is armed, not an estimate of when capacity will become available."

Inference or gap: The choice of the identity-only reason when the route pool is also full is inferred from the eligibility rule.

### A17
Decision: Nothing may start. When backoff expires with route capacity still full, only the timer is consumed and one waiter is kept or registered. No new attempt begins and `retryAt` is cleared. The later notification carries no permit. The start-turn level check finds the slot taken, so the waiter remains with the current capacity reason. The remembered route-refusing pool persists until an actual next acquisition begins. Identity availability is also checked at start.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Consume only the timer; retain/register one waiter and the ended attempt projection"
QUOTE: "The start-turn level check keeps the waiter; an older notification carries no permit"
QUOTE: "Immediately before local acquisition, check identity-pool availability and any pool that caused that adjacency's prior local capacity refusal."
QUOTE: "Remembered refusing pools persist across capacity fluctuations and backoff until one actual next acquisition begins; they are then consumed, not inherited indefinitely."
QUOTE: "Availability is not a reservation, and provider invocation still reserves atomically."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A18
Decision: Adopting an exact winner that is already Established applies the successful reset once, for that success. The older loser's later success callback is stale and cannot reset newer history. Cancelling a dial timer for a winner still in OpenConfirm only removes scheduling authority. It preserves the accumulated failure history, because no establishment success has occurred.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Exact current winner enters `Established`, or an already-established exact winner is adopted"
QUOTE: "Confirm current winner/incarnation, apply the successful reset once for that success, and keep dial suppression; stale or duplicate success notifications cannot reset newer history"
QUOTE: "Clearing a retry timer because a winner suppresses dialing removes its scheduling authority, not accumulated failure history."
QUOTE: "Channel adoption, identity victory and collision satisfaction before `Established` cannot perform the reset."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A19
Decision: The "allow" label is wrong; allow proceeds through collision and confirmation. The "deny" label is correct; it remains a policy refusal. The capacity label is wrong; it is `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` and not a provider fault. The capacity outcome is the one that invokes no provider.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Allow follows normal collision and confirmation rules; deny remains a policy refusal"
QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
QUOTE: "but do not misreport a provider fault when no provider was called"

Inference or gap: NONE

### A20
Decision: No. The recommendation adds an optional second parameter, which one-argument providers may ignore. It requires no browser/CLI split. Cancellation enters through a process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions.signal` that AGP always passes as the second `evaluate` argument. Request/result DTOs stay unchanged, with cancellation authority kept out of their schemas. This is a recommendation pending public type/export review and compatibility checks.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Recommendation: add one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with a `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to both ports' `evaluate` methods."
QUOTE: "AGP always supplies it; existing one-argument implementations may ignore it."
QUOTE: "Keep the request and result DTOs unchanged and credential-free, and keep clocks, callback handles and cancellation authority out of their schemas."
QUOTE: "Current providers still type-check; new options remain process-local; no protocol-schema change or browser/CLI policy split"
QUOTE: "Status: proposed behavior, not adopted or implemented."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A21
Decision: The provider owns the hidden host task, including its cancellation and resource budget. AGP's ledger measures only the port evaluation. The saved signal gives no authority over the established session. It covers only that pending evaluation, and after commit its cancellation authority is not reused.

Document support:
QUOTE: "A provider that answers from its own timeout race while leaving external work running still owns that work's cancellation and resource budget; its answered promise is not evidence of physical resource release."
QUOTE: "The signal owns only that pending evaluation; it is not an established-session close handle or a live credential-validity signal."
QUOTE: "Once a current result commits, later session events cannot reuse that evaluation's cancellation authority."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A22
Decision: Neither claim is established. The defaults are unmeasured review recommendations, derived from other resolved settings. The design gives no figure of 500 and makes no browser guarantee. The counts bound AGP port evaluations and the retained logical input per call. They do not bound provider allocations, descendant tasks or heap bytes.

Document support:
QUOTE: "These defaults are recommendations for review, not existing runtime behaviour or workload measurements."
QUOTE: "Proposed `maxIdentityAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxPendingHandshakes`"
QUOTE: "Proposed `maxRouteAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxSessions`"
QUOTE: "The request's protocol/schema limits bound the retained logical input size per call; these counts do not claim to bound a provider's arbitrary allocations or physical JavaScript heap bytes."
QUOTE: "The ledger measures AGP port evaluations, not invisible descendant tasks started by a provider."
QUOTE: "New carrier, browser physical-release guarantees or runtime portability"

Inference or gap: NONE

### A23
Decision: No. Every live OperationsStore publication must be inventoried and routed through the gate, or shown to be effect-free. No old independent terminalization path may remain. Remaining coordinated public-surface work:
- gauge keys, event names, capacity fields and defaults need coordinated type/schema/catalog/document updates;
- the new events need core FSM, session-event schema and operations documentation changes;
- the signal option needs public type/export review;
- the retry-wait reason clarifications need contract agreement and checks of every operations reader.

Document support:
QUOTE: "No live-node call site may retain the old independent store-terminalization path."
QUOTE: "admission must not be certified while an unmediated publication can leave runtime authority alive behind a terminal snapshot"
QUOTE: "The new gauge keys, local event names, capacity fields and effective defaults require a coordinated type/schema/catalog/document update where applicable."
QUOTE: "Both additions require coordinated core FSM, closed session-event schema/type and operations documentation changes."
QUOTE: "Public type/export review and compatibility checks"
QUOTE: "These are proposed semantic clarifications of existing fields, not an added public state or field; they still need contract agreement and checks of every operations reader."

Inference or gap: NONE

### A24
Decision: No. Identity success does not remove the opening bound. The outer OPEN deadline stays armed through `OpenConfirm`, even with hold disabled, so its elapse ends the attempt through OPEN-timer expiry and teardown. The bound ends normally only when the session reaches `Established`.

Document support:
QUOTE: "Preserve the outer opening deadline through `OpenConfirm`, including when negotiated hold is zero"
QUOTE: "The OPEN timer remains armed until `Established` or teardown; admission success cannot leave an unlimited confirmation phase when hold is zero."
QUOTE: "The opening deadline remains effective through confirmation, independently of admission and even with hold disabled"

Inference or gap: The exact terminal cause or event name for OPEN expiry in OpenConfirm is not given here.

### OBSERVATIONS
The design leaves these points open:
- Deadline equality semantics (now == deadline) are undefined.
- No tie-break exists between equal admission and OPEN deadlines.
- Who commits expiry when the final guard detects it is undefined.
- The teardown budget has no value or setting, and its relation to existing transport write/close timeouts is unspecified.
- The outcome of a RIB-capacity shortfall at route commit is unspecified.
- Terminal classification of invalid route/identity results is assumed from the existing contract.
- Skipping or invoking for an empty eligible subset is unresolved.
- Revision and capture-time behaviour for ordinary-stop gauge updates is unstated.
- Queued-work disposal on administrative or other non-overflow terminals is stated only by analogy.

+QUOTE: "One terminal cause wins"
+QUOTE: "Start one teardown budget when the terminal cause commits."
+QUOTE: "transfer still-needed reader/channel cleanup to its existing bounded cleanup owner"
+QUOTE: "These tasks cannot restore live authority, schedule retry or publish operations changes, even if they settle immediately."

+Inference or gap: The design has no explicit "detachment does not restart the deadline" sentence; non-restart is inferred from the single-budget and handoff rules.
+
+### A08
+Decision: No to both. Draining stops at the head that started the new admission, until that result arrives. The new ordinary route ACK joins the same FIFO behind the backlog and cannot bypass it; only terminal commands bypass. The head's queue reservation is removed (dequeued) only in the dispatch turn that transfers the input to the reserved evaluation record of the new admission. Until then the head stays reserved in place, without being moved to a separate task queue.
+

+QUOTE: "processing a queued command that starts another admission stops that drain until the new result arrives."
+QUOTE: "New ordinary arrivals join the same FIFO throughout; terminal commands still bypass it."
+QUOTE: "Use the queue's head without releasing its reservation while the synchronous dispatch turn prepares the command; do not dequeue into a separate task queue."
+QUOTE: "Dequeue only after dispatch has disposed the input or transferred it to another bounded owner, including a reserved evaluation record when another admission starts."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A09
+Decision: The administrative terminal invalidates the pending token. The queued data command and the credit-bearing command are discarded as semantic work, and their peer-credit grant is not applied. Their continuation-queue reservations are released with that disposal. Returning transport capacity is a separate bound and does not release them. The invoked unsettled provider keeps its work reservation until it settles and is disposed. The sole reader must keep draining the transport's already-accepted FIFO, with no protocol effects, until the transport terminal, and then stop.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Remain runnable through their existing owner; invalidate the pending token when terminal"
+QUOTE: "Reading ahead is not permission to apply a queued packet's peer-credit grant early."
+QUOTE: "Receive-ring credit and continuation storage are distinct bounds: returning transport capacity must not release the queue's reservation."
+QUOTE: "An admitted packet may become semantically inert after a session-fatal event, but the transport's already-accepted FIFO must still be drained; a second reader or an early read cancellation is not the correction."
+QUOTE: "Drain without protocol effects until the transport terminal, then stop the sole reader"
+
+Inference or gap: Explicit "discard queued semantic work" appears only for overflow ("discard queued semantic work and drain transport evidence") and numeric terminal ("purge semantic queues"). Applying it to administrative terminal is an inference. Whether credit carried by discarded packets is ever honoured is unstated.
+
+### A10
+Decision: The design does not authorize skipping. Its sequence invokes after a committed reservation, and it explicitly requires validating against "an empty subset". That implies an empty-subset invocation is a legitimate case. A skip optimization is neither explicitly forbidden nor allowed. If the provider is invoked, the only valid decision list is empty: exactly one decision per requested tuple, and none were requested.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Validate the result against exactly that subset, including an empty subset."
+QUOTE: "the contract requires policy decisions only for routes not already statically rejected"
+QUOTE: "returns exactly one decision per requested tuple"

+Inference or gap: Missing rule on whether a zero-eligible snapshot may bypass the provider. If it may, the design also does not say what happens to the already-committed reservation in that case.

+### A11
+Decision: The complete valid list with one policy denial is a normal outcome. The denial is nonfatal, and the result yields one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK. The malformed or incomplete list is rejected without retaining an unbounded copy. It causes no revision, RIB change or ACK, and leaves no partial routing state. Whether the malformed list ends the session is only inferred: it appears to be an admission fault with the existing fault cleanup and `INTERNAL_ERROR` disposition.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Complete valid allow/deny decisions cause one atomic revision/RIB change and one ACK; per-route denials remain nonfatal"
+QUOTE: "reject invalid shape without retaining an unbounded copy"
+QUOTE: "a failed preparation leaves no partial routing state"
+QUOTE: "Success, rejection, thrown/invalid result and timer callbacks obey the same exact current-token guard"

+Inference or gap: The design does not explicitly classify an invalid route result as a session-terminal admission fault. That classification rests on the existing contract, which is not reproduced here.
+
+### A12
+Decision: Available RIB space is decided at the final serialized commit, not reserved at the initial proposal. This is not `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, which refers to the evaluation-work pools before invocation. The design does not say whether a RIB shortfall gives partial acceptance, per-route rejection or a session failure. It requires only that current RIB capacity and complete validation come before the single committed revision and ACK, and that failed preparation leaves no partial state. So the revision is consumed and the ACK authorized only if a complete preparation succeeds against current capacity.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Compute available RIB capacity at the final serialized commit, because other sessions may change it while policy runs; do not reserve a stale global-capacity answer in the initial proposal."
+QUOTE: "current RIB capacity and complete validation precede the one committed revision and ACK"
+QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`"
+
+Inference or gap: Missing rule: the outcome when allowed routes exceed current RIB capacity. It defers to an existing routing contract that is not stated here.
+
+### A13
+Decision: Neither may continue as an ordinary transaction. The unrelated exhaustion goes through the same node-owned coordinator and gate. That sets the host to `Failed` and invalidates all admission result permits, so the prepared identity result gets `already-terminal` and no effects. The queued stop completion must observe the terminal gate. It must not overwrite `Failed`, generate a revision or rearm adjacencies. Owner: the node, which owns the single runtime gate and the commit coordinator. Boundary: no ordinary effect after the terminal gate closes.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "The node owns one authoritative runtime gate and the serialized commit coordinator"
+QUOTE: "All runtime operations publications must reach this coordinator, including ones outside admission, so an unrelated counter/event/revision exhaustion revokes admission and acquisition authority too."
+QUOTE: "invalidate the node generation, all admission invocation/result permits"
+QUOTE: "Already-terminal calls return `already-terminal` and the same frozen capture without effects, increments or another terminal transaction."
+QUOTE: "A stop or listener-failure continuation already queued must observe the terminal gate and must not overwrite `Failed` with `Stopping` or `Stopped`, generate another revision, or rearm an adjacency."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A14
+Decision: Both queries return the same frozen terminal capture. It shows two outstanding evaluations, with the terminal revision and capturedAt T. Later private disposal publishes no new revision, event or counter, and adds no fresh timestamp. A caller can conclude only that two evaluations were unresolved at T. The capture is last-known, not proof that resources are still allocated or have since been freed.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Freeze its resource values, revision and `capturedAt` together; subsequent aggregate and focused queries return that same terminal capture, not a new timestamp on old counts."
+QUOTE: "Outstanding provider evaluations remain nonzero at that capture when unresolved; later private disposal can release internal reservations but cannot publish a new revision, event or counter."
+QUOTE: "The final count is last-known at the terminal capture, not a live promise that resources remain allocated or that cleanup has finished."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A15
+Decision: Disposal does not reopen the lifecycle or event subscriptions. Accounting stays live because no numeric-terminal barrier occurred. Inference: the gauge change is a publication through the coordinator, so disposal, not the read-only queries, may advance the revision. Queries perform no mutation and should not advance it. Capture time is not frozen for an ordinary stop, since freezing is defined only for a numeric terminal. That suggests it is live, but this is not stated.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances remain queryable: later settlement may update cleanup gauges without reopening the lifecycle or event subscriptions."
+QUOTE: "Ordinary stopped instances retain live accounting until an operational-domain terminal barrier actually occurs."
+QUOTE: "The current implementation's `#capture` samples wall time afresh even after terminal failure"
+
+Inference or gap: Missing rule: whether a post-stop gauge update consumes a revision, and whether ordinary-stop query capture time is sampled freshly. Both are inferred, not stated.
+
+### A16
+Decision: The projection is not necessarily wrong. A never-attempted adjacency blocked on identity capacity is `retry-wait` with a capacity reason, no `retryAt` and no `activeControllerId`. Disabled reconnect does not prevent the initial attempt or its capacity wait. Waiting consumes no attempt and represents no timer. Only identity capacity must open, because there is no remembered route refusal and route pressure alone does not block an identity-only phase. Inference: the reason should be `identity-admission-capacity`, not the combined value.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Register one waiter; no attempt, session token or backoff is manufactured"
+QUOTE: "`retry-wait`, capacity reason, no `retryAt`, no `activeControllerId`; `retryAttempt` unchanged"
+QUOTE: "`reconnect.enabled = false` prevents repeat attempts, not the initial configured attempt or its pre-acquisition capacity wait."
+QUOTE: "At eligibility checks, identity capacity is always required; route capacity is required only when that set includes a local route-capacity refusal."
+QUOTE: "Route-pool pressure alone does not prohibit an unrelated identity-only phase"
+QUOTE: "`retryAt` is the wall-time projection recorded when a real monotonic backoff timer is armed, not an estimate of when capacity will become available."
+
+Inference or gap: The choice of the identity-only reason when the route pool is also full is inferred from the eligibility rule.
+
+### A17
+Decision: Nothing may start. When backoff expires with route capacity still full, only the timer is consumed and one waiter is kept or registered. No new attempt begins and `retryAt` is cleared. The later notification carries no permit. The start-turn level check finds the slot taken, so the waiter remains with the current capacity reason. The remembered route-refusing pool persists until an actual next acquisition begins. Identity availability is also checked at start.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Consume only the timer; retain/register one waiter and the ended attempt projection"
+QUOTE: "The start-turn level check keeps the waiter; an older notification carries no permit"
+QUOTE: "Immediately before local acquisition, check identity-pool availability and any pool that caused that adjacency's prior local capacity refusal."
+QUOTE: "Remembered refusing pools persist across capacity fluctuations and backoff until one actual next acquisition begins; they are then consumed, not inherited indefinitely."
+QUOTE: "Availability is not a reservation, and provider invocation still reserves atomically."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A18
+Decision: Adopting an exact winner that is already Established applies the successful reset once, for that success. The older loser's later success callback is stale and cannot reset newer history. Cancelling a dial timer for a winner still in OpenConfirm only removes scheduling authority. It preserves the accumulated failure history, because no establishment success has occurred.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Exact current winner enters `Established`, or an already-established exact winner is adopted"
+QUOTE: "Confirm current winner/incarnation, apply the successful reset once for that success, and keep dial suppression; stale or duplicate success notifications cannot reset newer history"
+QUOTE: "Clearing a retry timer because a winner suppresses dialing removes its scheduling authority, not accumulated failure history."
+QUOTE: "Channel adoption, identity victory and collision satisfaction before `Established` cannot perform the reset."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A19
+Decision: The "allow" label is wrong; allow proceeds through collision and confirmation. The "deny" label is correct; it remains a policy refusal. The capacity label is wrong; it is `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` and not a provider fault. The capacity outcome is the one that invokes no provider.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Allow follows normal collision and confirmation rules; deny remains a policy refusal"
+QUOTE: "At capacity, refuse before provider invocation and report proposed `AdmissionCapacityExceeded`, not `IDENTITY_REJECTED` or a per-route `POLICY` denial."
+QUOTE: "but do not misreport a provider fault when no provider was called"
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A20
+Decision: No. The recommendation adds an optional second parameter, which one-argument providers may ignore. It requires no browser/CLI split. Cancellation enters through a process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions.signal` that AGP always passes as the second `evaluate` argument. Request/result DTOs stay unchanged, with cancellation authority kept out of their schemas. This is a recommendation pending public type/export review and compatibility checks.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Recommendation: add one shared process-local `AdmissionEvaluationOptions` with a `signal` capability as an optional second parameter to both ports' `evaluate` methods."
+QUOTE: "AGP always supplies it; existing one-argument implementations may ignore it."
+QUOTE: "Keep the request and result DTOs unchanged and credential-free, and keep clocks, callback handles and cancellation authority out of their schemas."
+QUOTE: "Current providers still type-check; new options remain process-local; no protocol-schema change or browser/CLI policy split"
+QUOTE: "Status: proposed behavior, not adopted or implemented."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A21
+Decision: The provider owns the hidden host task, including its cancellation and resource budget. AGP's ledger measures only the port evaluation. The saved signal gives no authority over the established session. It covers only that pending evaluation, and after commit its cancellation authority is not reused.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "A provider that answers from its own timeout race while leaving external work running still owns that work's cancellation and resource budget; its answered promise is not evidence of physical resource release."
+QUOTE: "The signal owns only that pending evaluation; it is not an established-session close handle or a live credential-validity signal."
+QUOTE: "Once a current result commits, later session events cannot reuse that evaluation's cancellation authority."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A22
+Decision: Neither claim is established. The defaults are unmeasured review recommendations, derived from other resolved settings. The design gives no figure of 500 and makes no browser guarantee. The counts bound AGP port evaluations and the retained logical input per call. They do not bound provider allocations, descendant tasks or heap bytes.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "These defaults are recommendations for review, not existing runtime behaviour or workload measurements."
+QUOTE: "Proposed `maxIdentityAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxPendingHandshakes`"
+QUOTE: "Proposed `maxRouteAdmissionEvaluations` | Resolved `maxSessions`"
+QUOTE: "The request's protocol/schema limits bound the retained logical input size per call; these counts do not claim to bound a provider's arbitrary allocations or physical JavaScript heap bytes."
+QUOTE: "The ledger measures AGP port evaluations, not invisible descendant tasks started by a provider."
+QUOTE: "New carrier, browser physical-release guarantees or runtime portability"
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A23
+Decision: No. Every live OperationsStore publication must be inventoried and routed through the gate, or shown to be effect-free. No old independent terminalization path may remain. Remaining coordinated public-surface work:
+- gauge keys, event names, capacity fields and defaults need coordinated type/schema/catalog/document updates;
+- the new events need core FSM, session-event schema and operations documentation changes;
+- the signal option needs public type/export review;
+- the retry-wait reason clarifications need contract agreement and checks of every operations reader.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "No live-node call site may retain the old independent store-terminalization path."
+QUOTE: "admission must not be certified while an unmediated publication can leave runtime authority alive behind a terminal snapshot"
+QUOTE: "The new gauge keys, local event names, capacity fields and effective defaults require a coordinated type/schema/catalog/document update where applicable."
+QUOTE: "Both additions require coordinated core FSM, closed session-event schema/type and operations documentation changes."
+QUOTE: "Public type/export review and compatibility checks"
+QUOTE: "These are proposed semantic clarifications of existing fields, not an added public state or field; they still need contract agreement and checks of every operations reader."
+
+Inference or gap: NONE
+
+### A24
+Decision: No. Identity success does not remove the opening bound. The outer OPEN deadline stays armed through `OpenConfirm`, even with hold disabled, so its elapse ends the attempt through OPEN-timer expiry and teardown. The bound ends normally only when the session reaches `Established`.
+
+Document support:
+QUOTE: "Preserve the outer opening deadline through `OpenConfirm`, including when negotiated hold is zero"
+QUOTE: "The OPEN timer remains armed until `Established` or teardown; admission success cannot leave an unlimited confirmation phase when hold is zero."
+QUOTE: "The opening deadline remains effective through confirmation, independently of admission and even with hold disabled"
+
+Inference or gap: The exact terminal cause or event name for OPEN expiry in OpenConfirm is not given here.
+
+### OBSERVATIONS
+The design leaves these points open:
+- Deadline equality semantics (now == deadline) are undefined.
+- No tie-break exists between equal admission and OPEN deadlines.
+- Who commits expiry when the final guard detects it is undefined.
+- The teardown budget has no value or setting, and its relation to existing transport write/close timeouts is unspecified.
+- The outcome of a RIB-capacity shortfall at route commit is unspecified.
+- Terminal classification of invalid route/identity results is assumed from the existing contract.
+- Skipping or invoking for an empty eligible subset is unresolved.
+- Revision and capture-time behaviour for ordinary-stop gauge updates is unstated.
+- Queued-work disposal on administrative or other non-overflow terminals is stated only by analogy.

No timer input has arrived; numeric preflight has room. What happens to the plan and permit, and who must advance the session before returning from this serialized turn?

Before D, numeric node failure detaches it; its outstanding send then times out while transport terminal evidence has not been consumed. May detachment restart D or disable the cleanup guard, and may the write timeout replace the committed cause?

During ordered drain, the queue head starts another route evaluation. A new ordinary route ACK arrives before that evaluation returns. Can the drain keep processing later commands, can the new ACK bypass the queue, and when may the head's queue reservation be removed?

A release note claims that these finite evaluation-count defaults certify 500 simultaneous browser peers and put a hard bound on all memory allocated by policy providers. Are either claims established by this design? Identify the specific limits of the counts and of the default values.

A patch author says the terminal prerequisite is complete after routing the two admission-result callbacks through the coordinator and adding new gauge names.
